The orthography in the language is really weird, because of the way the native script works. As a consequence, /n/, and all other nasals, is represented as a digraph of the relevant stop consonant and an <e>. If you wanted to make /bɛ/, then you'd write <bé>, instead. It's just really weird orthography, is all. Also, the apostrophes make different sounds because of the letters on either side. As a general rule, if the preceding sound is a fricative, and the next sound is a consonant, then apostrophes make a /a/ sound. If the sound after the apostrophe is a vowel, then it makes no sound, unless the sound preceding it is a vowel, in which case it makes a glottal stop.
Oh, yeah. to form the subjunctive of the verb, you break up the digraphs. "Would have" would be translated into "dayaúdé", which would be pronounced /dajaudɛ/.

It would be nice if you could specify subverses to crosspost to when there is topical overlap. The way I'd like to see it work is there is a main subverse for the post, and then you can specify additional ones to crosspost to. The crossposted posts would show up in their respective subs with something after the title mentioning that it was crossposted from somewhere else. Also, the crossposted posts would link to the discussion in the original subverse so the discussion isn't so fragmented, and it would be governed by its posting/voting rules. Also, the list of crossposted subs should be able to be edited after the initial submission.

There may well be reasons this is a bad idea like spam or something but it's something I'd always wished reddit had and now that I don't care about that thing, it would be nice to see that happen here if possible.

Edit: Just a thought but maybe where it says like "(self.politics)" it could say "(crosspost.politics)" where politics would be the subverse with the main post.
